text:
maria: Hey team, seeing a weird install/import break after upgrading our Python SDK in a customer env. They installed redwood SDK wheel, app starts but imports fail with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood_core'" and API calls return 401 right after. Suspect path/packaging weirdness. Repro steps below.

josh: Can you paste pip freeze and how they installed? Also which python (pyenv/venv/system)?

maria: Repro steps from customer (condensed):
```
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install --upgrade pip
.venv/bin/pip install /tmp/redwood_sdk-2.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
# app imports: from redwood_core.client import Redwood
# ImportError: No module named 'redwood_core'
# but `pip show redwood-sdk` reports package installed
```
They're using pyenv 3.10.8 (system build), no user site packages allowed.

maria: pip show output they sent:
```
Name: redwood-sdk
Version: 2.1.0
Location: /home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages
Files:
  redwood_sdk-2.1.0.dist-info/*
  redwood_core/__init__.py -> ??? (missing at runtime)
```

maria: Notice Location is user site even though they installed into a venv path. Also they have a locally named repo folder called `redwood_core` in their project root (legacy internal module). My hunch: import resolution or sitecustomize is rewriting sys.path to prefer project root, or wheel shebang/entry points installed a script that mutates path.

kevin: @maria can you confirm sys.path at runtime? Ask them to run: `python -c "import sys, pprint; pprint.pprint(sys.path)"` inside venv and attach. Also check `python -c "import importlib, pkgutil; print(list(pkgutil.iter_modules()))[:20]"` to see top-level names.

maria: They ran sys.path and sent back snippet: 
```
['', '/home/ubuntu/project', '/usr/lib/python3.10', '/usr/lib/python3.10/lib-dynload', '/home/ubuntu/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages', '/home/ubuntu/project/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages']
```

maria: Note `/.local/...` appears before venv site-packages. That explains why pip show shows user install and why runtime can't find package (different name collision). They also have a `sitecustomize.py` in their project that does `sys.path.insert(1, os.path.expanduser('~/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages'))` (customer admits they put this in to workaround a different tool). So ordering is messed up.

josh: Yikes. So two issues: user-site being pulled ahead of venv, and a local repo folder `redwood_core` colliding with the official package name. Which is causing the 401?

maria: 401 likely separate: their installed wheel is older (2.0.x) in user-site and contains a different token handling that breaks auth header formatting. Runtime imports the wrong version (from user-site), so calls go out with malformed header -> 401.

kevin: Recommended repro/fix steps to send to customer: short checklist:
- Remove the user-site install: `pip uninstall redwood-sdk --user` and `rm -rf ~/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood*`
- Disable sitecustomize temporary (or set PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1) when using venv to ensure venv site-packages wins
- Ensure no local package name collisions (rename their `redwood_core` folder or use package namespace)
- Reinstall wheel inside venv: `.venv/bin/pip install --force-reinstall /tmp/redwood_sdk-2.1.0-py3-none-any.whl`

maria: Sent that to customer. They tried `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 .venv/bin/python -c "import redwood_core; print(redwood_core.__version__)"` and got `2.1.0` (good) and API started returning 200 again.

tara: Great root cause: environment/path hijack via sitecustomize + leftover user-site older egg. Can we add a short KB entry/FAQ in support? Also maybe update our wheel metadata to warn if imported from user-site & version mismatch?

maria: +1 on KB. I also added to repro notes: common symptom is 401s immediately after package upgrade with ModuleNotFound or wrong package loaded. Patch suggestion: our CLI could log a warning if package __file__ path is outside virtualenv (heuristic).

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-2026 created and escalated to eng-oncall.

kevin: tagging @eng-oncall for visibility — will follow up about warning in CLI and packaging notes.

maria: marking resolved for the customer; they removed the stray user-site package and disabled sitecustomize. Leaving this thread open for KB/docs tasks. :white_check_mark:
